pr_body:
This PR does two related things.
1. Removes the update available check from `extension list` command. It was slow and made what should be a simple command less usable.
2. Introduces as `--dry-run` flag to `extension upgrade` command. This option combined with the `--all` flag gives the user the same functionality as the old `extension list` command functionality, except now the update available checking has to be explicitly asked for and is better aligned in the `extension upgrade` command.

Closes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4220
pr_comments: @mislav I updated this PR if you want to take another look 🙇. The increased logic exercising meant passing around the `dryRun` variable to more functions, what are your thoughts on just adding the `dryRun` state as a property on the extension manager? I think this approach would work well as it would make it easier to add dry run flags to other extension commands.
@mislav Updated the PR to reflect the addition of `dryRunMode` as a property of the extension manager.

issue_context.title: `gh extension list` is very slow
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Listing the installed extensions seems to be extremely slow.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```console
$ time gh extension list
gh branch          mislav/gh-branch              
gh clean-branches  davidraviv/gh-clean-branches  
gh clone-org       matt-bartel/gh-clone-org      
gh user-stars      korosuke613/gh-user-stars     

real	0m8,439s
user	0m0,204s
sys	0m0,080s
```

I can replicate this multiple times.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Since the extensions are installed locally, I'd expect the listing of installed extensions to be very fast, e.g.

```console
$ time ls -1 /home/waldyrious/.local/share/gh/extensions/
gh-branch
gh-clean-branches
gh-clone-org
gh-user-stars

real	0m0,001s
user	0m0,001s
sys	0m0,000s
```

Maybe there should be a command-line option to toggle whatever slow step is taking place when listing the extensions?
comments:
Listing extensions is slow because it checks on GitHub for every extension whether it has updates (i.e. has newer commits pushed) https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/99cbfd3dd8ea32a27b9545e6ada56a1f4732e90b/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L104-L107

We could probably speed it up by avoiding doing this check too often.

> We could probably speed it up by avoiding doing this check too often.

IMO the default behavior should be to not do this check by default, and maybe print a message if the last check was too long ago, suggesting the user to run `gh extension list --check` (or whatever other flag name would be acceptable). That way, the slow behavior would be opt-in and deterministic, rather than "smartly" snuck in in some invocations of the command and not in others.

Hey @samcoe — I have had the chance to test gh 2.1.0, but even with this check for updates now done concurrently (thanks to #4396), it is still taking me several seconds to see the output (even more than before, ironically — although of course network latency variations will affect the results). As the original reporter, I would not consider this issue resolved until the times are much closer to a plain listing of `~/.local/share/gh/extensions/`. Please reopen the issue.

@waldyrious Thanks for the update that you are still experiencing this issue. I will reopen it. As next steps for speeding this up I think the only real option is to try to reduce the number of network requests. Two options there are to do caching and only checking for updates every 24hr (for example) or introducing a flag that specifies that `extension list` should or shouldn't check for updates as you mentioned in your previous comment. We could also do a combination of both where the new flag will force a update check otherwise only check for updates on a specified interval. 

@mislav @vilmibm What are your thoughts?

review_comments: This is a small change in existing behavior, I feel like it is nicer to print out the actual version change.
